# Opposing Factions — Rival Answers to the Crisis

The protagonist's party embodies one answer to the world's crisis — radical humanism,
mutual aid, teaching, repair ([[allegory]]). It cannot be the only answer on offer. The
antagonist is the ruling class, but the *argument* is crowded: other non-elite groups
carry their own diagnoses and their own cures, and several of them are wrong in ways
that cost lives.

## The requirement
> status: ratified (D-0092)

There must be opposing views on how to resolve the world's conflicts, held by groups
who are not the ruling class — rival non-elite philosophies with their own wants. The
trio is one faction among several contending answers, not the lone light against the
dark. Encoding this keeps the story out of the purity trap the [[allegory]] forbids: the
resistance is plural, and it disagrees with itself.

## Three sketched rival philosophies
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch of three non-elite rival movements (all names AI-coined, placeholders
pending the naming oracle and Q-0002):

- **The Red-Thread Skalds** — accelerationists who weaponize the Mother-Tongue to sever
  rather than heal, deliberately raising storms to drown the keeps regardless of who
  else drowns. The collapse-accelerationist / eco-fascist reading: they would sacrifice
  the very vellum-scrapers and drowned-parish poor the protagonist is trying to save,
  which is the friction — her radical humanism against their arithmetic of acceptable
  loss.
- **The Barrow-Cults** — isolationist hoarders who seal hidden sanctuaries behind dense
  knot-wards and stockpile clean soil, seed, and lore, turning refugees away at the
  door. The prepper / lifeboat-ethics reading: they hold axioms the protagonist may
  desperately need, forcing a consent-versus-need dilemma — she will not take by force
  what Frith says must be given freely.
- **The Slate-Menders** — complicit reformers who quietly fudge the empire's math to
  soften a quota here and there while leaving the order itself intact. The green-washing
  / harm-reduction-compliance reading: they fear the protagonist's hope as the most
  dangerous thing in the valley, and may betray her to protect the fragile mercy they
  have negotiated.

## Design note
> status: ratified (D-0033, D-0092)

These rivals are the shades-of-gray mandate (D-0033) worked out at the level of
factions: people doing bad things, or insufficient things, from inside real
constraints, not cartoons. They also enforce the anti-purity politics of the
[[allegory]] — the protagonist's answer has to win the argument against sympathetic,
coherent, wrong alternatives, never against strawmen. None of the three names or their
specific doctrines is ratified; only the requirement that such rivals exist.
